transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Well… I guess I’m here because I’ve been avoiding things. My workshop, mostly. And family get-togethers if my brother-in-law might be there. I’m tired of having to plan around all that.
Do you feel anxious when you think about attending these family get-togethers or going to your workshop?

Yeah… I do. Mostly because I know I’ll end up trying to avoid it. If my brother-in-law might be there, I just don’t go. Same with the workshop… I stay away from it. I’m just tired of arranging everything around not running into those reminders.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I don’t know… not like that, I don’t think. I get uneasy, sure, but I can’t say it suddenly peaks like you’re describing.
Do you have any recurring, unwanted thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?
Yeah… sometimes. It’ll just pop in, out of nowhere. I’ll see his hand with that heavy tool again, like a picture in my head. Could be when I’m shaving or painting. Makes my chest tighten a bit.
Are the things you're avoiding related to a specific traumatic event?
Yes… it’s tied to that one thing. I’ve been avoiding my workshop, and any family gathering where my brother-in-law might be. I’m just… tired of planning around all those reminders.
Are you avoiding these situations because you're afraid of having a panic attack or some other intense fear response while you're there?
I don’t think it’s about a panic attack, no. I just… don’t want to be around it, or him. I’d rather not put myself there.
Are you avoiding your workshop because it reminds you of the traumatic event or because you're afraid something bad will happen there?
It’s more that it reminds me of it. The workshop, and then family things where he might show up… I just keep steering clear of all that. I’m tired of having to plan around it.
Is it specifically your brother-in-law that you're trying to avoid, or is it also the places themselves that bother you?

It’s both, I guess. Him, mostly… but the workshop too. Places like that just bring it all back, so I’ve been keeping away from them and from family things where he might be. I’m worn out from working around it all.
Is avoiding your brother-in-law more about what he might do or say, or about the memories he brings back?

More the memories, I think. I mean… I don’t want to deal with what he might say either, but mostly seeing him—or being in the workshop—just brings it all back. I’m tired of planning everything around avoiding those reminders.
Is it the actual workshop itself that you're afraid of, or is it just the memories that the workshop brings back?

It’s not that I think the workshop is dangerous or anything. It’s… what it brings back. I end up staying away from it, and from family get-togethers if my brother-in-law might be there. I’m just tired of planning around all those reminders.
Is avoiding the workshop and family gatherings more about trying to prevent the memories from coming back or about preventing something bad from happening in those situations?

More to keep the memories from coming back. I don’t really think something bad is going to happen there… I just end up staying away from the workshop, and family things if he might be there. I’m tired of having to plan around it.
For how long have you been avoiding your workshop and family gatherings?
Since that confrontation with my brother-in-law… about two years and four months ago, I guess.
Has avoiding your workshop and family gatherings caused problems in your relationships or daily life?

Yeah… some. I still get by day to day, but I stopped doing the volunteer things that used the workshop, and I skip bigger family events more than I should. My painting’s been off and on too, since most of my supplies are out there.
Have you noticed any significant distress in your life due to avoiding these reminders?

Yeah… I’d say so. It’s not like everything’s falling apart, but it bothers me. I came in because I’m tired of steering clear of my own workshop and family get-togethers just to avoid running into those reminders. After this long, it feels like I’m planning my life around it.
Have you experienced any problems in your relationships with family or friends due to your avoidance of certain situations?

Yeah… a bit. I still manage the regular stuff, but I’ve dropped some volunteer jobs because they used the workshop, and I tend to stay away from the bigger family things. My painting’s gotten spotty too, since most of what I need is out there.
Have you avoided other activities or places beyond your workshop and family gatherings because they remind you of the traumatic event?
Not really much beyond that. It’s mostly the workshop… and family things where my brother-in-law might be there. That’s what I keep working around, I guess.
Have you ever felt like your avoidance of the workshop and family gatherings is so severe that it's significantly impacting your ability to function in daily life?

I wouldn’t say I can’t get through the day. I still handle the basics. But… yeah, it’s gotten in the way. I stopped doing some volunteer things if they’re tied to the workshop or big family events, and my painting’s kind of on and off now because most of my supplies are out there.
Would you say that avoiding the workshop and family gatherings has significantly reduced your participation in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I’d say it has. I still get by with the day-to-day things, but I’ve stopped doing some of the volunteer work I used to do when it involves the workshop or those bigger family events. And my painting… that’s been more off and on, since most of what I need is kept out there.
